records.issue_text: [BUG] For i >= 10 the test calls idpRep.getConfig().put(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC, ...) on a freshly constructed IdentityProviderRepresentation whose config map was never initialized, throwing NullPointerException. records.issue_text: [BUG] getForLogin() constructs IdentityProviderListQuery with a six-argument constructor (loaded, cacheKey, realm, searchKey, cached, query) and reads cache.getCurrentCounter(), but neither this 6-arg constructor nor a getCurrentCounter() method on RealmCacheManager is added by this diff, so the code does not compile against the repository as changed. The build fails with 'cannot resolve constructor IdentityProviderListQuery(Long, String, RealmModel, String, Set, IdentityProviderListQuery)' / 'cannot resolve method getCurrentCounter()' unless the accompanying storage PR that adds those members is merged first — an unstated prerequisite, so this diff cannot build standalone.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache key cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode) does not include organizationId, so a second getForLogin call with a different organizationId hits the existing query entry whose getIDPs(searchKey) returns null, then unconditionally invalidates the shared cache entry and replaces it — meaning the previously cached organization's result set is evicted on every alternating-organization access. In multi-organization realms (any login page for org A followed by login page for org B), the login cache is invalidated and repopulated on every request, causing a delegate (DB) hit per login page render and defeating the cache the PR exists to add; correctness is preserved only via the always-fresh reload.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup for the second created IDP ("idp-alias-20") also uses the wrong alias literal "alias". The IDP created at step 1 is never removed, and the cleanup lambda hits a non-existent resource, throwing during cleanup execution.
records.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, after creating the IDP with alias `"idp-alias-20"`, the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);`, i.e., it uses the literal key `"alias"` instead of `"idp-alias-20"`. This means the newly created IDP is not cleaned up, and the cleanup attempts to remove a (likely) non-existent IDP named `"alias"`, which can fail during cleanup execution.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] update() derives its invalidation decision from idpById = getById(model.getInternalId()), which is served through the cache, so registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate compares the updated model against a possibly-stale cached original rather than the persisted state. When a prior update on another node has not yet propagated the invalidation, the cached 'original' can match the updated model on all predicate-relevant fields (enabled, hideOnLogin, org link), so the update skips invalidating the login cache keys even though the stored row actually changed login eligibility — cluster-wide stale login IDP lists until the cache entry expires by revision; the invalidation decision should be computed from the delegate (source of truth), as the alias-invalidation path in the same method already risks.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Login-cache invalidation is only triggered from create/update/remove on this provider, but organization-to-IDP link changes that flow through OrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider without a subsequent provider-visible update leave the cached login ID lists stale. An admin unlinks a broker from an organization (or toggles its org link) via org-management endpoints that bypass this provider's update path; users on the login page continue to see the stale cached IDP (or miss a newly public one) until an unrelated invalidation occurs — a stale-authorization-style exposure where the login surface shows brokers the operator removed.

records.issue_text: [BUG] getLoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without a null guard on the config map, NPE-ing for any organization-linked IdentityProviderModel whose config is null. An org-linked IDP deserialized from the Infinispan cache or constructed by an extension with a null config map makes getLoginPredicate throw NullPointerException; in the cache provider this NPE fires inside create()/update()/remove() via registerIDPLoginInvalidation, breaking IDP management operations, and inside getForLogin, breaking the login page with a 500.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When a cached IdentityProviderListQuery exists but lacks the current searchKey, the code calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and then addRevisioned with cache.getCurrentCounter(), which other cluster nodes can race with: a node that already fetched the old query between the invalidateObject and the addRevisioned re-caches against a stale snapshot, and the update-time invalidation skip (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returning early) then leaves the org-scoped stale list in place. In a multi-node cluster, a login-IDP update that the skip condition considers non-invalidation-worthy (e.g. alias-only change) coinciding with an org-scoped cache expansion can serve a stale org login list to users until some other operation invalidates the key; single-node tests like testCacheIDPForLogin cannot exercise this window.
